e5490087e7.substituent_description: Left benzene ring (circle) carries a CH2 (leading to NH-C(=O)-CH2-N(iPr)-C(=O)-CH2-) at one carbon, F on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, and Cl on the next carbon after that (meta to the CH2, ortho to the F), i.e. 2-F, 3-Cl relative to the CH2. The chain ends on the N of a bicyclic indole-like ring (5-ring with N and a C2=C3 double bond; fused 6-ring drawn with a circle) that has Ac on C3 and a CH2-C(=O)-N group at C5 of the benzo ring, where the N belongs to a 6-membered ring (N, CH2, CF2, CH2, CH2, CH2) carrying two F on the carbon beta to N (3,3-difluoro).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Cl label is rotated and hand-written, reads as Cl
exact ring positions of Cl on the left ring and of the CH2 substituent on the indole benzo ring are read from rough freehand hexagons
e5490087e7.notes: Three C=O drawn as double bonds plus one C=C in the five-membered ring of the indole-like unit; no stereo marks. Atoms bearing no label are skeletal vertices.

003b281edc.substituent_description: A pyrrolidine N is bonded to a C(=O) which is bonded to NH-CH2-CH2- attached to one N of a piperazine; the other piperazine N is attached to a para-disubstituted benzene (circle) whose other para position carries O-CH2 joined by a hashed bond to C4 of a 1,3-dioxolane. The dioxolane C2 carries a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring (Cl ortho and Cl para to the attachment) and a hashed bond to a CH2 that is bonded to N1 of an imidazole ring drawn with two explicit double bonds.
003b281edc.notes: Double bonds: one C=O (top), two in the imidazole ring. Benzene rings drawn with circles, imidazole with explicit double bonds. Two hashed bonds, both on the dioxolane ring carbons; no wedge and no written stereo labels.

8e0448b408.substituent_description: A purine-like fused bicycle: the 6-ring (circle inside, two ring N) has COOtBu on the carbon between the two N and NH2 on the carbon adjacent to one ring N; the 5-ring (one N=C double bond drawn) has its ring N bonded through a solid wedge to a cyclohexane carbon. On the cyclohexane, going round from that N-bearing carbon: the next carbon carries BocNH via a hashed bond, and the carbon para (1,4) to the N-bearing carbon carries a hashed bond to a vertex that is joined by a plain bond to CO2H (reads as CH2-CO2H).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: hashed bond to the right side ends at a vertex before a plain bond to CO2H, so it is unclear whether a CH2 is intended
solid wedge between the five-ring N and the cyclohexane is thick and blurs into the N label
8e0448b408.notes: Six-ring drawn with an aromatic circle while the five-ring uses one explicit double bond. Handwritten; letters COOtBu and CO2H legible.

03e4153f2b.substituent_description: Chain from the top: H2N-C(=O)-HN-CH2-CH2-CH2 (the last bond is a solid wedge) to a nitrogen written N with H below it; that N is also bonded to a C(=O) that carries a carbon bearing iPr (solid wedge) and NHBoc, and to a CH2-C(=O)-HN- group joined to a benzene ring (circle). On the benzene ring, taking the HN-bearing carbon as 1: CH2OH at position 4 (para) and CH2-N(Me)-C(=O)-O-CH2- at position 3 (meta to HN, ortho to the CH2OH); the CH2 of the carbamate is bonded to C9 of a fluorene (two benzene circles plus a five-membered ring).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: the nitrogen written N with H beneath it has three carbon bonds (wedge-bonded chain carbon, a C=O and a CH2) in addition to the H label
benzene ring substitution positions read from a freehand hexagon
Boc written as Boc in NHBoc; hand-lettering is slightly small
03e4153f2b.notes: Two solid wedges: one from the carbon bearing iPr, one from the chain CH2 to the N(H). Four C=O drawn as double bonds (urea, valine-type C=O, glycine-type C=O, carbamate). OH written as OH on the CH2OH; Me written on the carbamate N.

988abb63de.substituent_description: A 3,4-difluorophenyl ring (F on two adjacent carbons, meta and para to the NH-bearing carbon) is bonded through NH to a C(=O) that is attached to a CH carrying a hashed-bond methyl and an O-C(=O)-CH2-CH2- ester; that chain ends on the N of a 3-oxo benzoxazine ring (N, C=O, CH2, O fused to a benzene ring).
988abb63de.notes: Typeset. Double bonds: three C=O plus three Kekule C=C in each of two benzene rings. One hashed bond (to a methyl); no stereo letters.

b2ffb616b2.substituent_description: A CH carbon carries NHBoc (plain bond up) and MeOOC (hashed bond to the left) and is bonded to a CH2 that attaches to a benzene ring; the ring carries OPh at the para position relative to the CH2.
b2ffb616b2.notes: Typeset. Benzene drawn with three Kekule double bonds. The only stereo mark is the hashed bond to MeOOC.

2fe459ecfd.substituent_description: A para-disubstituted benzene (circle) carries AcNH on one carbon and S(=O)2 on the carbon opposite (para); S is bonded to N, which bears Bn and a CH2-C(=O)-NH-N=CH- chain. The CH is bonded to C3 of a five-membered ring with one N and two explicit C=C bonds, with methyl stubs on the two ring carbons next to the ring N (2,5-dimethyl, so the CH= is on C3), and that ring N is bonded to a benzene ring (circle) bearing two methyl stubs (ortho and para to the ring N).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: the bond from the sulfonamide N to Bn has a bend (extra vertex) so it could be read as N-CH2-Bn
right-hand aryl ring is near the image edge; methyl positions (ortho and para) read from short stubs
NH written as N with H below it
2fe459ecfd.notes: Double bonds: two S=O, one C=O, one N=CH, two in the five-membered ring. Methyl groups are unlabeled line stubs (four stubs: two on the five-ring, two on the right benzene). Bn label is written as Bn.

3c5298bd36.substituent_description: A five-membered ring with two N (one carrying Me, two explicit C=C/C=N bonds) is bonded to a benzene ring (circle); going round the benzene from that carbon (position 1): NH at position 4 (para) and OEt at position 5 (ortho to NH, meta to the first substituent). The NH is bonded to a ring N of a fused bicyclic (two six-membered rings, ring N atoms in both) in which the other ring carries a methyl stub next to a ring N and, on the carbon on the other side of that ring N, a ring-N-bonded four-membered ring with MeO and two methyl stubs.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: two lines cross at the four-membered ring carbon next to N (horizontal line from the left methyl stub to N crossing the vertical bond), so it is unclear whether it is a quaternary carbon with two methyls or two crossing bonds
NH is joined to a ring N, giving an N-N bond as drawn
ring-atom vertices have small dots and the fused bicycle is freehand, so ring-N and double-bond positions are uncertain
3c5298bd36.notes: Handwritten; crossing lines make the top four-membered ring hard to interpret. Double bonds: two in the five-membered ring, three in one six-ring of the fused bicycle, one in the other six-ring. Methyl groups are unlabeled line stubs (one on the bicycle, two on the four-membered ring).

fc0fe786ea.substituent_description: A piperidine ring: the carbon at position 4 (opposite the N) bears EtO by a solid wedge, and the carbon next to N (position 2) bears a benzene ring by a hashed bond; the piperidine N is bonded to a CH2 attached to C4 of an indole. On the indole: MeO on C5 (next to the CH2-bearing carbon), a plain methyl stub on C7, and NH in the five-membered ring. The benzene ring has, taking the piperidine-bearing carbon as 1: O-CH2-CH2-NHAc at position 2 (ortho) and HO2C at position 4 (para).
fc0fe786ea.notes: Typeset. Aromatic rings drawn with Kekule double bonds: benzene 3, indole 4. Methyl on the indole is an unlabeled stub.
